analyst_view.overall: Sunderland are 18th with 9 points and host Jagiellonia in the Europa League on Thursday, three days before this, and on-loan Kevin Danso, who cannot face his parent club Tottenham, is reported (one report) to start that game. Regis Le Bris said on Wednesday that top scorer Brian Brobbey (thigh) and captain Granit Xhaka (calf) are improving but unlikely to play against Spurs, and Dan Ballard is also out. Tottenham are 10th under Roberto De Zerbi with four wins in five league games and a full week to prepare; no new injuries were reported, but Savio, Tel, Mudryk, Simons and Odobert are out. The numbers already take a big cut for Brobbey (about -23% on Sunderland's goals) and count Tottenham's heavy shooting lately and Peter Bankes' average card record.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals: 0.9 for Sunderland and 1.0 for Spurs, already lowered for Brobbey's absence and Sunderland scoring only 3 in six. Danso missing weakens Sunderland's defence a little and Spurs are fresher, but Spurs are short of wide forwards; these roughly balance, so I stay at about 1.9.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.6 corners, 5.2 for Spurs, already counting Tottenham's high corner count lately. A Sunderland side three days after a European game may sit back, which fits that split, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.6 cards, counting both sides' recent card counts and Peter Bankes' average record (4.0 a game). It is not a derby and no new bans or tensions stand out, so I stay at about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.8 shots, about even, with Tottenham's heavy shooting lately (+12%) already counted. Sunderland's Thursday game could tire them, meaning fewer of their own shots but more for Spurs; one report says Le Bris will rotate for Europe, which would soften that, so the split moves more than the total and I stay at about 24.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 7.8 shots on target, 4.3 for Spurs, already raised for Tottenham's accurate shooting and lowered for Sunderland's. Without Brobbey, Sunderland rely on Isidor or young Tutierov, which the numbers already reflect, so I stay at about 7.8.
